clinician.final_diagnosis: extrarenal Wilms tumor with favorable histology
clinician.trajectory_summary: 6-year-old girl presented with acute left upper abdominal pain and swelling, with a large heterogeneous abdominal mass distinct from the kidney seen on imaging. Histopathology of the mass showed characteristic Wilms tumor morphology (nests, cords, tubules of epithelial cells with spindle stromal cells) without anaplasia or invasion. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated positive nuclear WT1 staining and absence of residual kidney parenchyma in the tumor tissue, confirming extrarenal Wilms tumor with favorable histology.
